summary: The exact candidate is a verified partial parser correction: it normalizes schema-disambiguated arguments/args envelopes, including JSON-string and clean repeated wrappers, in one-shot and streaming paths. It does not fully resolve or verify the original model-level report, yet its committed report labels the outcome fixed. Request changes to narrow that claim and explicitly classify unresolved corruption and retry escalation.

tests.what_was_measured: On the recorded base, actual DeepSeekV4Detector one-shot and three-character streaming output retained every clean reported envelope. On the exact candidate, clean object, JSON-string, args, double-, and quadruple-envelope cases normalized; valid, schema-ambiguous, unknown, empty, and corrupt-string boundaries were preserved.
Candidate regression suite at the exact SHA: 10 tests and 6 subtests passed.
Complete pre-existing function-call parser suite at the exact candidate: 243 tests and 4 subtests passed.
Candidate-advertised combined parser command at the exact SHA: 253 tests and 10 subtests passed.

gpu_execution.evidence: One assigned AMD Instinct MI355X/gfx950 was inventoried, but the candidate is Python parser-only and the named DeepSeek V4 model weights were unavailable. No GPU result is used as evidence.

remaining_counterexamples: The reported mid-stream duplication/corruption of inner command text remains unchanged and is explicitly outside the candidate's repair behavior.
The reported corrupted quadruple-wrapped payload cannot be normalized when the inner JSON/string is syntactically damaged.
Schemas without a usable declared top-level property set retain an added envelope, by design.
remaining_limitations: DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Vision-Exp weights were unavailable, so generation frequency, vision/model semantics, and the error-feedback escalation loop were not reproduced end to end.
The available tiny Llama fixture is a different model architecture and was not used as substitute proof.
Only one gfx950 GPU was assigned; no multi-GPU or distributed behavior was tested.
No native source changed, so no native rebuild or compiler/ISA validation was applicable.

The candidate's retained historical parser-suite failure could not be reproduced: the isolated test, full pre-existing parser file, and advertised combined command all passed in the prepared environment.
